products.name: Flowise
products.note: Visual LLM workflow builder; low-code RAG; self-hosted; no-code agent building

reading.body:
Flowise is a self-hosted, open-source platform that lets teams build and deploy AI systems through visual workflows without writing code, positioning itself as a bridge between prototype and production.

The platform's architecture reflects a specific bet about AI adoption: that the bottleneck for many organizations is not access to models, but the ability to wire those models into retrieval systems, databases, and autonomous agents with minimal engineering. By packaging RAG, workflow composition, and agent-building into a single visual interface, Flowise targets the gap between prototype demos and systems that must run on premises or integrate with proprietary infrastructure. This matters for the AI stack because it suggests demand for abstraction layers that hide complexity from teams without deep machine learning expertise.

The data does not cover Flowise's compute consumption, infrastructure requirements, infrastructure dependency, or how its self-hosted model scales with user load. It includes two named use cases, neither of which reveals technical depth, resource intensity, or growth trajectory. The company has no visible patent filings, regulatory filings, or litigation in the record, which leaves open whether it faces any institutional barriers to adoption or if such barriers simply have not yet appeared.

profile_text.body:
Flowise is an open source generative AI development platform for building AI agents and orchestrating LLMs, according to its website. The company describes it as providing modular building blocks for agentic systems, ranging from simple compositional workflows to autonomous agents, with deployment on cloud or on-premises infrastructure that it characterizes as enterprise-grade.

The site's product listing covers Flowise itself, a visual LLM workflow builder in the coding and developer tools category. The description notes low-code retrieval-augmented generation, self-hosting, and no-code agent building. The site presents customer comments, including one from UneeQ saying it uses Flowise to orchestrate AI within its Synapse AI brain and that it reduced the resources needed to deploy digital human experiences.

No litigation, MCP server, SEC, or patent facts are recorded for the company.
